newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks dip below 600-point barrier.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks dip below 600-point barrier.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed below the psychological 600-point mark on Thursday, for the first time since the end of October, brokers said.
But turnover was up on foreign shedding of stocks to show year-end returns, they said.
The all share index closed 1.9 points down at 599.9 after hovering just above the 600 mark for nearly two weeks.
"(Dropping below the barrier) was almost a non-event," said Jardine Fleming HNB deputy general manager Deva Ellepola.
"It looked more like a psychological barrier when it was broken to go up (on October 30)."

Turnover shot up to 74.5 million rupees from 18.1 million the day before. It was supported by 233,200 Ceylon Brewery shares, up 75 cents to 33.75, 60,000 development bank DFCC at 289 rupees and 100,000 Aitken Spence at 117 rupees.

Turnover was fuelled mostly by foreign funds selling to show a reasonable return to shareholders at year's end, a broker for Bartleet Mallory said. Foreign sales on Thursday amounted to 49.5 million rupees while purchases were 42.2 million.
Brokers said they expected the market to fall further in the immediate absence of any good news to turn in around.
